state.label: El Niño Advisory · Record-Class Odds Favored
state.detail: El Niño is intensifying toward a potentially historic peak. The weekly Niño 3.4 reached +2.6°C in early August. NOAA's Aug 13 discussion puts very-strong odds above 90% for the Oct–Dec peak and, for the first time, a 69% chance the event exceeds every El Niño since 1950 (RONI ≥ +2.5°C).

narrative: NOAA's August 13 discussion escalated the event from very strong to potentially historic. The weekly Niño 3.4 index reached +2.6°C in early August — up from +2.1°C in mid-July, +1.7°C in June and +0.5°C in late May — while the official May–July ONI printed +1.39°C and RONI +1.0°C. The decisive new number is on strength: NOAA now assigns a greater-than-90% chance of a very strong peak in Oct–Dec and, for the first time, a 69% chance the event exceeds every El Niño back to 1950 on the relative index (RONI ≥ +2.5°C). The framing has flipped accordingly — the live question is no longer whether 2026 joins the Super club but whether it leads it, with a new all-time record now the central expectation rather than the tail. Atmospheric coupling is emphatic: the July SOI ran near −2.4 (about two standard deviations) and MEI.v2 hit +2.41, the highest June–July value in the record back to 1979. Real-world confirmation keeps arriving — NOAA holds below-normal Atlantic hurricane-season odds near 75%, and India's monsoon, after a severe June, recovered sharply in July to near-normal. The residual uncertainty is now narrow: the exact magnitude of the autumn–winter maximum and how far past the 2015–16 mark it prints.
